_disclaimer: DEMONSTRATION DATASET. Synthetically generated for portfolio purposes. These values were not measured on any instrument and do not describe a real sample.
_project: Comprehensive Characterization and Python-Based Data Analysis of Iron Oxide Nanoparticles (demonstration)

bands.assignment: O-H stretch: adsorbed molecular water + surface hydroxyls
Atmospheric CO2 asymmetric stretch -- INSTRUMENT ARTEFACT

uvvis.scattering_exponent_note: Effective exponent from an empirical lambda^-n fit over 780-900 nm. Real absorption persists in that window, so this is not a pure Rayleigh/Mie exponent and the corrected spectrum is turbidity-reduced rather than scattering-free.
uvvis.absorption_character: Broad, monotonically rising absorption from the NIR into the UV with no discrete excitonic maximum -- consistent with O(2p)->Fe(3d) charge transfer plus a strong sub-edge (Urbach) tail. This is why magnetite appears black.
uvvis.band_gap_verdict: NOT REPORTED AS A BAND GAP. Fe3O4 is a mixed-valence, near-metallic conductor above the Verwey transition, not a wide-gap semiconductor; and the spectrum is a scattering-contaminated dispersion measurement. The four equally defensible analysis choices below give values spanning 2.34 eV, and allowing for the choice of linear window the full defensible span is 0.64-3.00 eV. That is larger than any difference one would be trying to detect. Tauc analysis is shown here to demonstrate the method and its failure mode, not to extract a physical constant.

tga.atmosphere_assumed: N2 (inert) -- assumed, so NO oxidative mass gain

regions.assigned_process: Loss of physisorbed and interparticle water
Loss of strongly bound water and surface dehydroxylation (2 Fe-OH -> Fe-O-Fe + H2O)
Residual dehydroxylation / loss of lattice-associated OH
Comparatively stable; no further resolvable mass loss

step_deconvolution.note: Boundary-independent alternative to region integration. The summed amplitude exceeds the measured total mass loss because part of the lowest-temperature event occurs below the starting temperature of the run.

tga.thermal_stability_note: Above ~650 C the synthetic curve is flat to within balance noise, i.e. no further resolvable volatile loss in the assumed inert atmosphere.

technique_matrix.main_information: Crystal structure, phase identity, lattice parameter, crystallite size, microstrain
technique_matrix.quantitative_output: d-spacings; a = lattice parameter (A); D_Scherrer (nm); microstrain eps
technique_matrix.key_limitation: Volume-weighted and blind to amorphous or poorly-ordered material; cannot separate Fe3O4 from gamma-Fe2O3 on peak position alone; Scherrer size is a coherent-domain size, NOT a particle size

technique_matrix.probes: Vibrational modes -- local bonding and surface chemistry
technique_matrix.main_information: Fe-O lattice modes; adsorbed water; surface hydroxyls; presence/absence of organics
technique_matrix.quantitative_output: Band positions (cm-1); relative intensities; band areas (semi-quantitative at best)
technique_matrix.key_limitation: Heavily overlapped bands in the Fe-O region; absorptivities are unknown so intensities are not concentrations; sampling geometry (ATR vs KBr) shifts band positions and intensities

technique_matrix.main_information: Charge-transfer absorption; qualitative optical behaviour; dispersion stability
technique_matrix.quantitative_output: Absorbance vs wavelength; apparent Tauc intercepts (unreliable for this material)
technique_matrix.key_limitation: For a dispersion, measured absorbance mixes true absorption with Mie/Rayleigh turbidity; Fe3O4 is not a wide-gap semiconductor, so a Tauc 'band gap' is not a meaningful intrinsic property

technique_matrix.main_information: Particle/aggregate size, shape, degree of agglomeration, surface texture
technique_matrix.quantitative_output: Size distribution statistics: mean, median, SD, quartiles, D[4,3], D[3,2]
technique_matrix.key_limitation: Measures whole features, so aggregates are counted as particles; thresholding choices shift the mean by several percent; limited field of view creates sampling bias; conductive coating inflates diameters

technique_matrix.main_information: Volatile content: adsorbed water, surface hydroxyls, organics (if present); thermal stability
technique_matrix.quantitative_output: Mass loss per region (%); DTG peak temperatures (C); total volatile content (%)
technique_matrix.key_limitation: Gives mass change only, never chemical identity; results depend strongly on atmosphere, heating rate, sample mass and packing; in air, Fe3O4 oxidation causes a mass GAIN that can mask losses

size_comparison.interpretation: The SEM number-mean diameter (19.1 nm) exceeds the XRD coherent-domain size (11.9 nm) by a factor of 1.60; on a like-for-like volume-weighted basis the factor is 1.83. In the demonstration scenario this gap is what one would EXPECT, and it is informative rather than contradictory.
reasons_for_divergence: Different measurands: XRD reports the size of coherently diffracting domains; SEM reports the outline of a visible feature. A single SEM feature may contain several domains.

Different weightings: Scherrer sizes are volume-weighted while a raw SEM mean is number-weighted. Volume weighting emphasises the largest particles, so the two statistics are not comparable until one is converted (here D[4,3]).
Surface disorder: a structurally disordered or hydrated surface shell contributes to the SEM outline but diffracts incoherently, so XRD does not count it.
Agglomeration: touching particles are frequently segmented as one feature, inflating the SEM size.

Microstrain: if strain broadening is attributed entirely to size, the Scherrer size is systematically UNDERESTIMATED. Here Scherrer alone gives 11.1 nm while the Williamson-Hall separation gives 11.9 nm.
Imaging artefacts: conductive coating thickness and edge detection thresholds both bias SEM diameters upward.
size_comparison.complementarity: None of these techniques is a substitute for another. XRD establishes what the crystalline phase IS; SEM establishes how the material is physically organised; FTIR reports what sits on the surface; TGA quantifies how much of it there is; UV-Vis reports the optical consequence. A defensible characterisation requires the set, and phase assignment in particular should be confirmed by a magnetic or spectroscopic method (Mossbauer, Raman, XPS) rather than by XRD peak positions alone.
size_comparison.combined_xrd_tga_surface_coverage: Combining the XRD crystallite size (specific surface area 97 m2/g for equivalent spheres) with the Region II TGA mass loss gives 5.4 water molecules per nm2. That figure is in the range usually quoted for hydroxylated iron-oxide surfaces, which is a useful internal consistency check on the demonstration dataset.
